10. Despite a prestigious training at LAMDA and a breakout on the global stage under director Peter Brook, X found himself so disillusioned by the limited, stereotypical roles offered to him in 1970s Britain that he quit acting entirely. For several years, he returned to his home country to work as an editor and journalist, effectively vanishing from the industry.
He was only lured back to the screen by a sprawling historical epic that required his specific intellectual gravitas, a role he would eventually reprise years later for a 53-episode television series, Y.
This comeback proved definitive; in a single year (1984), he appeared in two of the world's biggest films: playing a high-ranking, sinister official in a Steven Spielberg blockbuster, and a pivotal role in David Lean’s final masterpiece. ID X and Y.
